seo.description: Explore Fes in Morocco. Discover top attractions, cultural landmarks, local cuisine, and essential travel tips for an unforgettable trip.

hero_subtitle: Morocco's Spiritual Heart — a Living Medina of Crafts, History, Flavours & Centuries of Tradition.

overview.title: Welcome to Fes, Morocco's Cultural Capital
overview.p1: Fes feels different from the moment you enter its old city. Inside Fes el-Bali, one of the world's great medieval urban areas, narrow lanes open onto quiet courtyards, neighbourhood mosques, artisan workshops and centuries-old buildings. It is a city to explore slowly, with no need to tick every sight off a list.
overview.p2: A trip to Fes is as much about atmosphere as monuments. You can spend the morning discovering historic madrasas, stop for a plate of fragrant tagine, watch craftsmen at work, then return to a traditional riad before heading out again in the evening. If you want to understand Morocco's history, architecture, crafts and food in one place, Fes is a natural stop on your itinerary.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Fes
places.subtitle: Historic schools, artisan quarters, viewpoints and quiet corners that reveal the character of Morocco's oldest imperial city.

fes_el_bali.title: Fes el-Bali
fes_el_bali.desc: The maze-like old city where souks, mosques, workshops and historic houses come together.

al_quaraouiyine.title: Al Quaraouiyine
al_quaraouiyine.desc: A historic centre of learning and one of the city's most important spiritual landmarks.

bou_inania.title: Bou Inania Madrasa
bou_inania.desc: Zellige, carved stucco and cedar details make this one of Fes's standout historic buildings.

nejjarine.title: Nejjarine Museum
nejjarine.desc: A beautifully restored funduq celebrating Morocco's woodworking heritage and traditional crafts.

chouara.title: Chouara Tannery
chouara.desc: One of Fes's best-known craft scenes, where leatherworking remains part of the medina's living economy.

bab_bou_jeloud.title: Bab Bou Jeloud
bab_bou_jeloud.desc: The famous blue gate is a natural starting point for exploring the old medina.

mellah.title: Fes Mellah
mellah.desc: Discover another layer of Fes through its historic Jewish quarter and surrounding royal district.

marinid_tombs.title: Marinid Tombs Viewpoint
marinid_tombs.desc: Come around sunset for one of the most memorable panoramic views over the medina.

itinerary.title: A Relaxed 3-Day Fes Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A simple first-timer route that leaves room for getting lost in the medina — because in Fes, that is often part of the experience.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Start at Bab Bou Jeloud
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter the medina early while the lanes are calmer. Follow the main streets towards the historic heart, stopping at small bakeries, spice shops and artisan stalls along the way.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Visit Bou Inania Madrasa and continue through the souks toward the Nejjarine area. Take your time rather than trying to cover every lane.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Head to a rooftop for tea and a view over the rooftops, then enjoy dinner in or around the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Explore the city's historic learning and religious architecture, including the area around Al Quaraouiyine and the old neighbourhoods surrounding it.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: See the traditional tanneries, browse leather workshops and visit the Nejjarine Museum. Fes is one of the best places in Morocco to see crafts still made by hand.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Try a traditional Moroccan dinner and leave some time for a quiet walk around the illuminated medina streets.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Pick a trip based on your interests: Volubilis and Moulay Idriss for history, Meknes for imperial architecture, or Ifrane and the Middle Atlas for a change of scenery.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Allow enough time to return without rushing. If you stay in the city, use the afternoon for shopping or a final visit to a favourite café.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Finish with mint tea and a final view of Fes as the lights come on across the medina.

stays.title: Where to stay in Fes? Our Favorites
stays.subtitle: From luxurious historic palaces and boutique riads in the medina to modern hotels in the Ville Nouvelle.

card1.name: Palais Amani
card1.desc: An exceptional luxury riad featuring an edible garden, fine dining, exquisite suites, and peaceful courtyards in the heart of Fes el-Bali.

card2.name: Hotel Sahrai
card2.desc: A contemporary 5-star hotel perched on the hillsides with stunning panoramic views over the old medina, infinity pool, and world-class Givenchy spa.

card3.name: Riad Fes
card3.desc: A stunning architectural masterpiece blending Moorish design and modern comfort, offering breathtaking rooftop vistas and refined hospitality.

booking_banner.title: Explore all stays in Fes
booking_banner.desc: Compare real-time rates, read verified guest reviews, and enjoy free cancellation on traditional riads, authentic dars, and modern hotels.

eat.title: What to Eat in Fes
eat.subtitle: Fes is a rewarding city for food lovers, from simple medina kitchens to polished Moroccan dining rooms.

fassi.title: Fassi Cuisine
fassi.desc: Look for dishes such as pastilla, slow-cooked tagines, harira and seasonal salads. Fassi cooking is often known for its balance of sweet, savoury and fragrant spices.

medina.title: Medina Food Stops
medina.desc: Follow your appetite through the medina: bakeries, soup counters, grilled meats, olives, dates and fresh juices can make an excellent informal lunch.

rooftop.title: Rooftop Tea
rooftop.desc: For a slower evening, choose a rooftop terrace overlooking the old city and order mint tea alongside a traditional dinner.

cooking.title: Cooking Experiences
cooking.desc: A local cooking class or market visit can be a fun way to understand the ingredients and techniques behind Moroccan home cooking.

sweets.title: Sweet Treats
sweets.desc: Try Moroccan pastries, chebakia and almond-based sweets with coffee or tea when you need a break from sightseeing.

order.title: What to Order
order.desc: If it is your first visit, ask your host or server what is freshly prepared that day. Fes rewards curiosity more than a fixed checklist.

shoes.title: Wear Comfortable Shoes
shoes.desc: The old city is best explored on foot. Expect uneven paving, steps and plenty of walking.

stay.title: Stay Inside or Near the Medina
stay.desc: A riad gives you a more immersive experience, while staying just outside the medina can be easier if you prefer taxis and wider roads.

guide.title: Use a Local Guide if You Want Context
guide.desc: Fes has many layers of history and a guide can add context, especially on a first visit. If you go independently, save your accommodation location offline.

cash.title: Carry Some Cash
cash.desc: Keep Moroccan dirhams for small purchases, cafés, taxis and market stalls even if your hotel or larger restaurant accepts cards.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Fes
daytrips.subtitle: Fes is also a useful base for exploring the history and landscapes of northern and central Morocco.

volubilis.title: Volubilis
volubilis.desc: Explore the Roman ruins, mosaics and open landscapes of one of Morocco's best-known archaeological sites.

moulay_idriss.title: Moulay Idriss
moulay_idriss.desc: A hillside pilgrimage town with whitewashed streets and views across the surrounding countryside.

meknes.title: Meknes
meknes.desc: Combine your Fes stay with a visit to another imperial city, known for monumental gates and historic architecture.

ifrane.title: Ifrane & Middle Atlas
ifrane.desc: Head into the Middle Atlas for cedar forests, cooler air and a completely different landscape from the medina.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Fes?
q1.answer: Two full days can cover the main sights, but three days gives you time to explore the medina without rushing and add a nearby day trip.

q2.question: Is Fes a good destination for a first trip to Morocco?
q2.answer: Yes, especially if you are interested in history, architecture, crafts and Moroccan food. The medina is intense and busy, so a slower pace makes the experience easier.

q3.question: What is the best area to stay in Fes?
q3.answer: Stay in or near Fes el-Bali if you want atmosphere and easy access to the historic sights. Ville Nouvelle is more convenient if you prefer modern hotels, wider roads and easier vehicle access.

q4.question: Can I visit the Fes medina without a guide?
q4.answer: You can explore independently, although the medina is large and easy to navigate imperfectly. A guide can be useful when you want deeper historical context or help discovering less obvious places.

q5.question: What should I eat in Fes?
q5.answer: Try Fassi specialities such as pastilla and traditional tagines, along with Moroccan salads, soups, pastries and mint tea. Ask locally what is fresh that day.

q6.question: What are the best day trips from Fes?
q6.answer: Volubilis, Moulay Idriss, Meknes and Ifrane are among the easiest additions to a Fes itinerary, depending on whether you prefer archaeology, history or nature.

content.hero_subtitle: Discover the authentic charm and unique experiences of Fes.
content.sec1_text: Located in one of Morocco's most picturesque regions, Fes offers visitors an immersive journey into rich heritage, stunning architecture, and warm local hospitality.
content.sec2_text: Whether you are exploring historical sites, tasting traditional Moroccan flavors, or discovering surrounding natural landscapes, Fes provides memorable moments for every traveler.
content.sec3_text: To make the most of your visit to Fes, plan your itinerary during optimal seasons, connect with certified local guides, and experience authentic local accommodations.
